content_of_post_to_comment: I see a lot of people say “you’re allowed to be bad at things before you get good.” Which is true. But I also just wanted to say you’re allowed to be bad at something, never get good at it, and keep doing it anyway
comment: There’s an interesting difference between persistence aimed at mastery and persistence aimed at meaning. Some pursuits matter not because they improve us, but because they keep us connected to a part of ourselves.
